node_definition.done_when: First confirm at base that each half reproduces, and record it as the base arm: a run with a manifest aged past the alarm threshold and a stream written seconds ago is classified or displayed in alarm, and a wait whose probe is echo pending is accepted as a probe. In a new tests/test_a_wait_ages_on_its_stream.py: a run with a stale manifest and a fresh stream is not in alarm; a run with both stale is; a wait probe naming only echo pending or git rev-parse HEAD is reported as unable to fail; and a probe naming a pid, a job id, a port or a path is accepted. The named negative control (the age read from the manifest mtime again) is executed and fails the fresh-stream case. Fixtures use synthesised run directories under the test's temporary path, never the real pointer or run directories, and the test asserts the real pointer directory is untouched. Another live node edits the review reflex's resume path in reckon/crew/recovery.py; keep this change inside the wait classification, its vocabulary and the wait facts. The gate is the new test plus every existing test file whose name contains wait, run at base and at head; list the files in the manifest. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder; each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. Every pytest process uses a basetemp private to that process. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/a-wait-ages-on-its-stream.html records the change. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: Land both halves of followup f-cot-the-wait-predicate-settled-by-three-corrections of crew-observability-truth as its body settles them, and leave expiry alone because the body marks it an unsettled design question. Half one: a declared wait is aged on the run's stream freshness rather than its manifest's mtime, or both ages are rendered, so a busy worker whose stream is fresh is never shown in alarm. Half two: a declared wait's probe counts only when its result can differ, meaning it references something outside the worker (a job id, a pid, a port or a path); a probe that cannot fail, such as echo pending or git rev-parse HEAD against exit 0, does not satisfy it. The body names the dead end that must not be repeated (requiring only that the probe runs and its terminal is reachable).
